sn12.12:1.2: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.
sn12.12:1.4: The nutriment edible food, gross or subtle; second, contact; third, mental volition; fourth, consciousness.
sn12.12:1.5: These are the four kinds of nutriment for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the assistance of those about to come to be.”
sn12.12:2.1: When this was said, the Venerable Moḷiyaphagguna said to the Blessed One:
sn12.12:2.2: “Venerable sir, who consumes the nutriment consciousness?”
sn12.12:2.3: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.
sn12.12:2.5: If I should say, ‘One consumes,’ in that case this would be a valid question:
sn12.12:2.7: But I do not speak thus.
sn12.12:2.8: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,
sn12.12:2.9: ‘Venerable sir, for what is the nutriment consciousness a condition?’ this would be a valid question.
sn12.12:2.10: To this the valid answer is:
sn12.12:2.11: ‘The nutriment consciousness is a condition for the production of future renewed existence. When that which has come into being exists, the six sense bases come to be; with the six sense bases as condition, contact.’”
sn12.12:3.2: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.
sn12.12:3.4: If I should say, ‘One makes contact,’ in that case this would be a valid question:
sn12.12:3.6: But I do not speak thus.
sn12.12:3.7: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,
sn12.12:3.8: ‘Venerable sir, with what as condition does contact come to be?’ this would be a valid question.
sn12.12:3.9: To this the valid answer is:
sn12.12:3.10: ‘With the six sense bases as condition, contact comes to be; with contact as condition, feeling.’”
sn12.12:4.2: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.
sn12.12:4.4: If I should say, ‘One feels,’ in that case this would be a valid question:
sn12.12:4.6: But I do not speak thus.
sn12.12:4.7: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,
sn12.12:4.8: ‘Venerable sir, with what as condition does feeling come to be?’ this would be a valid question.
sn12.12:4.9: To this the valid answer is:
sn12.12:4.10: ‘With contact as condition, feeling comes to be; with feeling as condition, craving.’”
sn12.12:5.2: “Not a valid question,” the Blessed One replied.
sn12.12:5.4: If I should say, ‘One craves,’ in that case this would be a valid question:
sn12.12:5.6: But I do not speak thus.
sn12.12:5.7: Since I do not speak thus, if one should ask me,
sn12.12:5.8: ‘Venerable sir, with what as condition does craving come to be?’ this would be a valid question.
sn12.12:5.9: To this the valid answer is:
sn12.12:5.10: ‘With feeling as condition, craving comes to be;
sn12.12:6.12: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.’
sn12.12:7.1: “But, Phagguna, with the remainderless fading away and cessation of the six bases for contact comes cessation of contact;
sn12.12:7.2: with the cessation of contact, cessation of feeling;
sn12.12:7.3: with the cessation of feeling, cessation of craving;
sn12.12:7.4: with the cessation of craving, cessation of clinging;
sn12.12:7.5: with the cessation of clinging, cessation of existence;
sn12.12:7.6: with the cessation of existence, cessation of birth;
sn12.12:7.7: with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.12:7.8: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
